title: Kenny Dorham's Backyard
venue_description:
Kenny Dorham's Backyard

East Austin outdoor stage

Kenny Dorham's Backyard at 1106 E. 11th Street is a beloved East Austin outdoor music yard tied to DiverseArts programming. Blue Monday Blues Jam and the monthly Jazz OUTside series with free jam keep participatory music at the center.

Expect blankets chairs BYOB energy food trucks and suggested-donation doors. It is neighborhood legacy music — blues jazz and community hang — under open sky rather than club lighting.

Players singers dancers and listeners all fit the yard culture. Check DiverseArts listings before weather-sensitive outdoor nights.

title: The Elephant Room
venue_description:
The Elephant Room

Downtown jazz club

The Elephant Room on Congress Avenue is Austin's classic downtown jazz basement. Serious listening and a deep local jazz lineage define the room.

Monday nights belong to Michael Mordecai's long-running jazz jam — sit-ins house rhythm and surprise guests. The club actively programs 2026 shows beyond the jam.

Arrive ready to respect the bandstand etiquette that keeps this hang legendary.

title: The Buzz Mill
venue_description:
The Buzz Mill

Riverside cafe and acoustic stage

Buzz Mill's Riverside location on Town Creek Drive runs around the clock and hosts a Monday Music Open Mic aimed at musicians singers and songwriters.

Acoustic guitars and a supportive PA-friendly room make it an easy walk-up mic. Signup at 7:00 PM; music 8:00–10:00 PM with local hosts.

A Riverside staple if you want cafe energy instead of bar-volume stages.

title: Batch Craft Beer & Kolaches
venue_description:
Batch Craft Beer & Kolaches

East Austin jam and open mic hub

Batch on Manor Road packs more open stages into one brewery than almost anywhere else in town. Sundays bring CTBA bluegrass and Golden Hour jazz; Mondays host AFTM folk open mic and classical reading nights; last Sundays add a supportive open mic; third Saturdays welcome Austin Choro Club.

The room stays community-first: drop-in pickers tip buckets and collaborative jams over VIP culture. Kolaches beer and acoustic instruments share the floor comfortably.

Start here if you want one address that maps Austin's participatory week across bluegrass jazz folk classical and Brazilian choro.

title: Cactus Cafe
venue_description:
Cactus Cafe

UT Texas Union listening room

Cactus Cafe remains one of Austin's historic songwriter rooms — now under University Unions on the UT campus. Tuesday Songwriters Open Mic is original-music only hosted by Jake Farr.

Free entry and a true listening-room ethic keep craft at the center. Performer signup runs through the host email; the night follows the academic calendar seasonally.

For singer-songwriters who want a quiet attentive room this is still essential Austin.
location: 2308 Whitis Ave Texas Union Austin TX 78712

title: Mozart's Coffee Roasters
venue_description:
Mozart's Coffee Roasters

Lake Austin Boulevard deck

Mozart's is known citywide for coffee lake views and Late at the Lake — a big Tuesday outdoor open mic that prioritizes original song debuts.

Separate signup sheets for originals covers and poetry keep the long performer list organized. Rules favor short sets without backing tracks or full drums.

Contact music@mozartscoffee.com; arrive early if you want a slot on a busy lakeside night.

title: Regal Rooms
venue_description:
Regal Rooms

South Austin Event Center

Regal Rooms hosts Brecks Blues — a collaborative Tuesday blues jam with professional backline from the Silver Alert Band. It continues a two-decade jam tradition in South Austin.

Signup at 7:30 PM; jam into the late evening. Free or pay-what-you-want support keeps the door friendly for players and listeners.

Come to plug in and play with others not to deliver a solo showcase set.

title: Lucky Rabbit
venue_description:
Lucky Rabbit

Jonestown acoustic open mic

Lucky Rabbit on Ranch Road 1431 serves the Lake Travis and greater Austin songwriter crowd with a Tuesday open mic hosted by Chris Slone.

Inclusive acoustic sets welcome vocalists who need accompaniment. Professional sound and a 6:00–9:00 PM window make it approachable for all levels.

Proof that Austin's open-stage map stretches well beyond downtown.

title: Poodies Roadhouse
venue_description:
Poodies Roadhouse

Spicewood Hill Country roadhouse

Poodies Hilltop Roadhouse carries decades of Texas music lore into present-day Wednesday open mics under the No Bad Days banner.

Country Americana and songwriter sets rule the night. Sign up near 7:30 PM; play without a fee on a stage that still feels like working Hill Country music.

Rotating hosts keep the mic lively for locals and Austin drivers willing to head west on 71.

title: Opa Greek Cafe
venue_description:
Opa Greek Cafe

South Lamar cafe and wine bar

Opa on South Lamar blends Greek cafe hospitality with a weekly Wednesday open mic. Music sits comfortably beside poetry and art in a neighborhood room.

In-person signup around 6:30 PM leads into a 7:00–10:00 PM show window. It is a friendly South Austin foothold for first-timers and regulars alike.

Check opasola.com/events for holiday shifts and special nights.

title: Tulum Botanical Bar
venue_description:
Tulum Botanical Bar

East 7th music open mic

Tulum Botanical Bar runs a Wednesday music open mic built for players — acoustic vocals experimental approaches and live looping included.

Signup from 7:00 PM; performances from 8:00. In-house recording and livestream claims make it attractive if you want a documented set without studio rates.

East Austin energy with a music-first weekly mic.

title: Monks Jazz Club
venue_description:
Monks Jazz Club

South Austin jazz room

Monks Jazz Club on East Saint Elmo Road is a purpose-built jazz venue with ticketed programming and a weekly Wednesday jam.

Daniel Dufour hosts most weeks from about 9:00 PM to midnight. No cover; one-drink minimum. Bring your instrument and settle in for a late sit-in often livestreamed.

Essential for Austin jazz players who want a real club jam after the early evening songwriter circuit.
location: 310 E. Saint Elmo Rd Austin TX

title: New World Deli
venue_description:
New World Deli

Guadalupe bluegrass open mic home

New World Deli on Guadalupe Street hosts Eddie Collins's monthly Bluegrass Open Mic listed through Austin Friends of Traditional Music.

Second Thursdays from 7:00 to 9:00 PM welcome bluegrass and old-time acoustic players. Show up with instruments and join a long-running traditional music night.

Central Austin's reliable monthly picking room for the AFTM community.
